title: A named source root goes unconfirmed mid-claim when a settled run's retained-run read or its publication doesn't finish: 'latest root-authority transition was not published'
outcome: A session whose root was confirmed keeps it confirmed unless a real authority change happened. If a root-authority transition is left unpublished, the host settles it or a supported call does, so evidence isn't withheld turn after turn, and a truly unsettled transition still can't be overtaken.
acceptance: The way a root's latest transition ends up not Published on a named, previously confirmed root is identified from source and shown by a deterministic test, or the investigation stops and reports that it can't be reproduced, with what was ruled out

After the fix that sequence ends with a confirmed root through an automatic or supported path, without a restart, a retry loop or a turn run only to recover: a turn opening inside it stays honestly unconfirmed and the next ordinary turn opens confirmed. A transition that truly remains unsettled still blocks credit.
The review pair is clean and behaviour tests cover both the recovery and the still-blocked case; no time-based assertions

completion.summary: A settled run's root no longer stays unconfirmed when its retained-run read or publication doesn't finish: the host settles it through the ordinary maintenance path, and the next ordinary turn opens confirmed. A truly unsettled transition still blocks credit. Field samples aren't shown to have taken this path.
